discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 030701
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
301 AM EDT Sat Oct 3 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Primarily dry conditions expected for the coming week.

- Cool on Saturday with highs in the 60s. Trending slightly
  warmer Sunday.

- Very crisp Tuesday morning with lows in the 30s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 240 AM EDT Sat Oct 3 2026

Much cooler this morning with clear skies and light northerly
winds allowing for ideal radiational cooling. Dew points in the
low to mid 40s across the area will keep lows close to these
values. Some patchy mist/fog will be possible but should remain
near surface and the light winds will help to mix drier air
keeping any mist/fog very localized. 

Highs today with mostly sunny skies will again be in the mid
60s. Lows tonight will run a degree or two cooler with slightly
drier air in place, however a weak trough moving eastward into
the region will allow for increased WAA ahead of the upper level
troughing and highs on Sunday will be warmer with highs slightly
warmer getting into the lower 70s across the area. In the wake
of the weak disturbance a northwesterly to zonal flow will
return across the region with synoptic cooling returning, lows
Monday morning back into the low to mid 40s and highs on Monday
only in the low to mid 60s. This pattern also brings a shot of
drier airmass into the region and will bring a crisp morning on
Tuesday with lows in the mid to upper 30s, BRRRRRRR. Should make
for good sleeping weather, may also want to plan on protecting
any very temperature sensitive plants/animals out of an
abundance of caution. Still thinking that some isolated frost 
on more elevated surfaces will be possible but with still very 
moist and warm soils should keep any frost development at bay. 
Will continue to keep an eye on this situation. With a more 
northwesterly flow into the later part of the week and slightly 
higher synoptic heights arriving dry conditions look to continue
with slight warming into the end of the week when highs 
Wednesday and onward into the 70s.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 116 AM EDT Sat Oct 3 2026

VFR conditions and light northerly winds expected through this 
TAF period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 030531

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1231 AM CDT Sat Oct 03 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are expected across the U.S. today.

   ... Synopsis ...

   A midlevel trough and attendant surface cold front are forecast to
   move east across the upper Mississippi Valley today. Increasing
   midlevel moisture with the large-scale ascent ahead of the trough,
   coupled with conditionally unstable midlevel lapse rates, should
   result in enough elevated buoyancy for thunderstorms across portions
   of the region. Given the elevated nature of this convection and
   otherwise limited instability, severe thunderstorms are not
   anticipated. 

   Farther southeast, a slow-moving front extending from the Carolinas
   southwestward toward the northwest Gulf will remain a focus for
   thunderstorm development through the period. Although ample moisture
   will support thunderstorms along and south of the boundary,
   generally weak vertical shear and modest lapse rates within the
   moist thermodynamic environment should limit prospects for organized
   severe convection.

   ..Marsh/Halbert.. 10/03/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 030533

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1233 AM CDT Sat Oct 03 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely across the USA on Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   On Monday, an upper low will deepen further as it moves east across
   Quebec, with strong cooling aloft spreading into the northeastern
   states. Behind this system, a large area of high pressure will exist
   from the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes into much of the southeastern
   states. Given northeasterly surface winds over those areas, the more
   robust low-level moisture will remain confined to the Gulf Coast
   states. Here, winds aloft will remain weak, with primarily
   non-severe storms expected.

   Elsewhere, relatively cool midlevel temperatures will exist over the
   Great Basin as a weak midlevel wave moves across NV/UT. This may aid
   isolated afternoon thunderstorms, with minimal severe potential.

   ..Jewell.. 10/03/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
